name: Lech Wałęsa
summary: Wałęsa led the independent Solidarity union and the nonviolent movement that ended communist rule in Poland, then as president pushed rapid privatisation, a market economy with a safety net, and Poland's entry into NATO and the European Union. He insists on separation of powers, a free press and term limits, and has been a hard critic of Russia and of Poland's later governments.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As president he oversaw the conversion to a free-market economy.

public-ownership.rationale: As president he oversaw conversion of the state-run economy to a market system.

unions-good.rationale: He spent his career founding and leading the Solidarity trade union, which won workers' right to organise freely.

decide-locally.rationale: In his inaugural address he called for decentralising the state so that as many decisions as possible are taken at the bottom, where people live.

central-planning.rationale: Says communist economics has not worked anywhere and cannot be realised.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Said Poland should become a nation of owners and everyone should be able to own part of national property.

one-party-rule.rationale: As Solidarity leader he refused a coalition with the communists and led the move to free elections, ending one-party rule.

separated-powers.rationale: Calls the separation of powers the most important thing his generation achieved and says Poland's current breaches of it follow Putin's direction.

party-controls-media.rationale: Says that without an independent press there are Putins; he defends a free press as a safeguard.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Says states can no longer cope alone, and that today's reason of state is taking part in building structures larger than a country, accepting that some national elements are lost.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Says elected positions should have one or at most two terms and blames Putin's system for allowing unlimited terms.

recall-officials.rationale: Says everyone elected should be removable at any moment, alongside one term at most, to stop mafias forming.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Says he worked as president for NATO to expand and for Ukraine and Belarus to join NATO and the EU.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Says Russia must withdraw from and return all territory taken from Ukraine.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Treats the separation of powers as the foundation of the Polish state and condemns the governing majority's infringement of it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Told young protesters defending judicial independence not to let the separation of powers be disturbed and promised to stand with them even if they are arrested.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Says everyone should be removable at any moment.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejects communism but keeps a market economy, corrected to deal with unemployment, as the way forward.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Declares he will never agree to imprisoning people for their convictions and demands release of those jailed for union and civic activity.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wants a free-market economy with other things improved and extra support for the unemployed; his office's programme named a social safety net for the weakest.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: As president he pushed NATO enlargement and had advocated Poland's membership.

term-limits.rationale: Says all elected positions should be for one term or at most two.

independent-unions.rationale: He negotiated and signed the 1980 Gdańsk agreement conceding independent, self-governing unions and led Solidarity.

farm-price-support.rationale: His office's programme allowed temporary public subsidies for farm goods and defended farmers with customs and credit policy.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Quotes with approval John Paul II's statement that the working man takes precedence over capital in the production process.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Urges all countries to press Russians by propaganda and leaflets to adopt a political system with three separated powers and a free press.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Says Ukrainians are fighting courageously for our principles and Ukraine must not yield a millimetre of occupied land.

notes: Uncertainty rule not met: searched church and state, religion, abortion, family and gender, minorities, immigration, nationalism, head of state and class themes in English and Polish interviews and found no stated position on most; those statements stay null. Searched economy, government, liberty, world and means themes. His 2013 remarks on gay MPs do not settle any statement; no primary statement on same-sex marriage turned up in searches, so those statements stay null. Many statements are outside what his speeches and interviews address.
